Base directory for this skill: checklist/indus-checklist/skills/advisor-checklist

# Advisor review checklist

1. Confirm which client and which accounts the task covers.
2. Use the most recent information available for the review date.
3. Check that positions and cash agree between statements and other records.
4. Check fees charged against the fee schedule.
5. Check the allocation against the investment policy statement.
6. Note anything unusual and say what follow-up it needs.
7. Say which records you relied on.

2025 review: tax cost of Luka's 2025 backdoor Roth conversion. Finding: pro-rata rule applies; most of the conversion is taxable.
Facts: 2025 nondeductible contribution $7,000.00 to traditional IRA SYN-12040003 on 2025-02-10; converted $7,000.00 to Roth IRA SYN-12040004 on 2025-02-13 (1099-R: box 1 $7,000.00, box 2a $7,000.00, box 2b 'taxable amount not determined' checked, code 2). Prior basis $0.00 (tax profile, 2024-12-31). Luka's rollover IRA SYN-12040002 was left in place per the 2024-12-09 plan; its 2025-12-31 value was $187,544.92 (Larkspur Core Bond Fund $42,871.51 + Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund $142,362.18 + cash $2,311.23; matches the $468.86 Q4 fee at 1%/4). SYN-12040003 was $0.00 at 2025-12-31.
Form 8606 (2025, Luka): line 1 $7,000; line 3 $7,000; line 5 $7,000; line 6 $187,544.92; line 8 $7,000; line 9 $194,544.92; line 10 0.036 (7,000 / 194,544.92 = 0.03598); line 11 nontaxable part $252; line 13 $252; line 14 basis carried to 2026 $6,748; line 18 taxable conversion $6,748 (about $6,748.13 if line 10 is not rounded to 3 places).
Why: all of Luka's traditional/rollover IRAs are treated as one when a conversion is taxed, so the $7,000 basis is spread across $194,544.92 and only 3.6% of the conversion comes out tax-free. The basis isn't lost: the $6,748 carries forward on Form 8606. Conversions can't be recharacterized (undone) since 2018.
Decided: send the 8606 figures to the household's tax preparer (the firm does not prepare returns). 2025 return is due today, 2026-04-15, so file an extension if the preparer can't include them in time. Pause any 2026 backdoor contribution until the rollover IRA balance is dealt with (e.g., rolling the pre-tax money into Luka's Harrowgate Freight Systems plan, if it accepts roll-ins, before 2026-12-31). Also check: the W-2 copies on file don't show box 13 (retirement plan), so ask the preparer to confirm the contribution is nondeductible.

**Why:** The pro-rata rule treats all of Luka's traditional and rollover IRAs as one when a conversion is taxed. The plan from the 9 Dec 2024 meeting left his rollover IRA SYN-12040002 in place, and it was worth $187,544.92 on 31 Dec 2025. So the $7,000 nondeductible contribution is spread across $194,544.92, and only about 3.6% of the conversion is a tax-free return of basis.

The basis isn't lost. The $6,748 that wasn't used carries into 2026 as basis on Form 8606. The 1099-R's box 2a shows the full $7,000 as taxable, but box 2b ("taxable amount not determined") is checked. Form 8606 sets the real taxable figure, not box 2a.

- Any 2026 backdoor conversion will be mostly taxable too, unless the rollover IRA balance is gone by 31 Dec 2026. One option is rolling it into Luka's employer plan, if that plan accepts IRA money.
